summary:
[  edit  ]
The Object  CHOP  compares two objects and outputs channels containing their raw or relative positions and orientations. The information that can be output is:
Position of one object relative to another
Rotation of one object relative to another
Bearing of one object relative to another
Single Bearing Angle between two objects
Distance between the origin of two objects
Inverse Square of the Distance between two objects
The optional two inputs allow you to compare X,Y,Z points in world space with objects or each other. The inputs are expected to have three channels containing XYZ points (three channels with the suffix x, y and z). Alternatively, they can be in the standard transform formats as described by the  Transform CHOP  help. These inputs replace the target and/or reference objects. Object and points can be compared with each other, but "Rotation" mode will always return zero.
See also the  SOP to CHOP  and the  Parameter CHOP . They retrieve other information from  objects  and  SOPs .

parameters.label: DAT  Table
parameters.name: dat
parameters.description: Uses a  Table DAT  to specify the target and reference objects to use. The first column will be the target objects while the second column will be the reference objects. No headers are used.

parameters.label: Target  Object
parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The object that is being compared to the position of the reference object. The Target Object can be expressed as a text string. This can be useful when the object name needs to be a variable - it allows you to type in a name which may include expressions or variables.

parameters.label: Reference   Object
parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The object that acts as the origin of the comparison. The  Reference  Object can be expressed as a text string.

parameters.label: Swap Target/ Reference
parameters.name: swaptargetreference
parameters.description: Swap the objects defined above in the Target Object and  Reference  Object parameters.

parameters.label: Compute
parameters.name: compute
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specify the information to output from the objects as described in the parameters below. Except for 'measurements', these match the standard transform formats as described by the  Transform CHOP .

parameters.label: Transform (Euler)
parameters.name: transform
parameters.description: A transform using euler (rx ry rz) for the rotation.

parameters.label: Transform (Quaternion)
parameters.name: transformquat
parameters.description: A transform using quaternion (qx qy qz qw) for the rotation.

parameters.label: 4x4 Matrix
parameters.name: mat
parameters.description: A 4x4 transform matrix.

parameters.label: 3x3 Matrix
parameters.name: mat3
parameters.description: A 3x3 transform matrix. This includes scale/rotation but no translation.

parameters.label: Measurements
parameters.name: measure
parameters.description: Enables the toggles below to select what to measure. Measurements give you one object's position relative to another. You get the XYZ of the origin of the Target Object relative to the origin and rotation of the  Reference   Object . That is, you get the XYZ of the target object's origin as if you were at the 0,0,0 location (origin) of the  Reference   Object , looking down the  Reference   Object 's Z-axis.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.name: translate
parameters.description: The displacement from the reference object to the target object.

parameters.label: Rotation
parameters.name: rotate
parameters.description: The orientation difference from the reference object to the target object.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: The scale difference from reference object to the target object.

parameters.label: Quaternion
parameters.name: quat
parameters.description: The quaternion from reference object to the target object.

parameters.label: Bearing
parameters.name: bear
parameters.description: The rotation necessary for the reference object to be facing the target object.

parameters.label: Single Bearing Angle
parameters.name: singlebear
parameters.description: An angle representing where the target object is relative to the reference object. Zero degrees is directly in front, 90 degrees is beside and 180 degrees is behind.

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: The distance between the two objects.

parameters.label: Inverse Square Distance
parameters.name: invsqr
parameters.description: The inverse squared distance between the two objects, useful for modeling electric forces, audio dropoff and gravity.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - The transform order to use for Rotation, Scale, Transform, Bearing, or Single Bearing Angle  Compute  modes.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - The rotation order to use for Rotation, Scale, Transform, Bearing, or Single Bearing Angle  Compute  modes.

parameters.label: Include Order Channels
parameters.name: includeorderchans
parameters.description: Turn on to include channels for Transform Order and Rotate Order.

parameters.label: Bearing  Reference
parameters.name: bearingref
parameters.description: ⊞  - Bearing requires a direction to use as a reference base.

parameters.label: Bearing Vector
parameters.name: bearing
parameters.description: ⊞  - An arbitrary base direction for the bearing calculation.

parameters.label: Point  Scope  X
parameters.name: tscopex
parameters.description: When one of the optional point inputs is connected, this determines which channels represent X, Y and Z.

parameters.label: Point  Scope  Y
parameters.name: tscopey
parameters.description: When one of the optional point inputs is connected, this determines which channels represent X, Y and Z.

parameters.label: Point  Scope  Z
parameters.name: tscopez
parameters.description: When one of the optional point inputs is connected, this determines which channels represent X, Y and Z.

parameters.label: Append  Attributes
parameters.name: appendattribs
parameters.description: Adds a rotate attribute to any rotation channels the Object  CHOP  creates.

parameters.label: Smooth Rotation
parameters.name: smoothrotate
parameters.description: When on outputs a smooth rotation curve without graphical jumps at 0, 90, etc.

localNotes.excerpt: Vértices: ◦ Cada primitiva tiene una lista de vértices. Un vértice es un índice que apunta a un punto en la lista de puntos. ◦ Los vértices también pueden tener atributos. • Atributos: ◦ Son cruciales para almacenar datos adicionales por punto, vértice o primitiva. ◦ Los atributos son la piedra angular del diseño de los POPs, permitiendo la creación, modificación, duplicación, cambio de nombre y eliminación de datos. ◦ Se almacenan de manera muy eficiente como Shader Storage Buffer Objects (SSBOs) en los GLSL POPs, lo que permite un procesamiento altamente paralelo en la GPU. ◦ Los atributos pueden ser de varios tipos de datos (float, double, int, uint) y tener de 1 a 4 componentes (como RGB o RGBA para color). También pueden ser matrices (mat2x2 a mat4x4) o arreglos de componentes. ◦ Los nombres de los atributos estándar de Derivative (como "P" o "Color") comienzan con mayúscula, mientras que se recomienda que los atributos definidos por el usuario comiencen con minúscula p

Practical Applications - **Rendering**: POPs drive 3D geometry with attributes like `Color` and `Normal`. - **Particles**: Points with attributes (e.g., `Vel`, `PartForce`) for simulations. - **Point Clouds**: Efficiently manage large datasets without TOPs’ 4-channel limitations. - **External Output**: Send data to lasers, DMX, or LEDs. ## 6. Workshop Plan ### Objective Equip participants with a solid understanding of POPs, their advantages, and practical use in TouchDesigner projects. ### Duration 2-3 hours, split into theory and hands-on segments. ### Structure #### Part 1: Introduction (30-45 minutes) - **What are POPs?** (10 min) - Definition, purpose, GPU benefits. - **POPs vs. SOPs** (15 min) - Key differences, when to use each. - **Core Concepts** (15 min) - Points, primitives, attributes, groups. #### Part 2: Hands-On Demos (1.5-2 hours) -
